title: An oil price shock in Velmar: AD-AS, the Phillips curves and the way back
scenario: Velmar, an invented country, is in long-run equilibrium with an unemployment rate of 5 percent, equal to its natural rate, and actual and expected inflation of 2 percent. Then a sudden, large rise in the world price of oil raises production costs for firms across Velmar.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Draw a correctly labeled AD-AS graph showing Velmar's long-run equilibrium, with LRAS, the price level PL1 and full-employment output YF. On your graph, show the short-run effect of the rise in the price of oil, labeling the new price level PL2 and real output Y2.

key.because: a rise in the price of oil, an input cost

slips.AD: Oil is an input cost for firms, so its price shifts SRAS, not AD.
slips.LRAS: A temporary jump in an input price changes short-run costs; it does not change the economy's resources or technology.

rubric.point: A correctly labeled AD-AS graph: Price level on the vertical axis, Real GDP (or real output) on the horizontal axis, a downward-sloping AD, an upward-sloping SRAS and a vertical LRAS, with the starting equilibrium at YF and PL1
accept: PL and Y as axis labels
Y1 at full employment if it is shown on LRAS
an arrow showing the leftward shift

rubric.point: The new short-run equilibrium where AD crosses SRAS2, with a price level PL2 above PL1 and real output Y2 below YF
accept: higher price level and lower output marked on the axes

parts.sample: The graph has Price level on the vertical axis and Real GDP on the horizontal axis. AD slopes down, SRAS1 slopes up, and LRAS is vertical at YF; AD and SRAS1 cross on LRAS at PL1 and YF. The rise in the price of oil raises firms' costs, so SRAS shifts left to SRAS2. AD now crosses SRAS2 at a higher price level, PL2, and a lower real output, Y2, to the left of LRAS.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Identify what happens to Velmar's unemployment rate in the short run.

rubric.point: States that unemployment rises above 5 percent (above the natural rate)

parts.sample: Real output falls below full employment, so Velmar's unemployment rate rises above its natural rate of 5 percent.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Draw a correctly labeled graph of Velmar's short-run and long-run Phillips curves. Label point A where the economy starts, at 5 percent unemployment and 2 percent inflation. On your graph, show the short-run effect of the rise in the price of oil on the curves, and label the economy's new short-run position B.

key.because: a negative supply shock (a rise in the price of oil)

slips.LRPC: The natural rate of unemployment has not changed, so LRPC stays at 5 percent; the supply shock shifts the short-run curve.

rubric.point: A correctly labeled graph: Inflation rate on the vertical axis, Unemployment rate on the horizontal axis, a downward-sloping SRPC and a vertical LRPC at 5 percent, with point A where they cross at 2 percent inflation

accept: an upward shift of SRPC, shown with an arrow

rubric.point: Point B on SRPC2 with inflation above 2 percent and unemployment above 5 percent
accept: B to the right of LRPC and above point A

parts.sample: The vertical axis is the Inflation rate and the horizontal axis the Unemployment rate. LRPC is vertical at 5 percent. SRPC1 slopes down and crosses LRPC at point A, at 2 percent inflation. The oil price rise is a negative supply shock, so SRPC shifts right to SRPC2. Point B is on SRPC2, to the right of LRPC and above A: unemployment is above 5 percent and inflation is above 2 percent.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Assume Velmar's government and central bank take no action. Explain how Velmar's economy returns to its long-run equilibrium. In your answer, say what happens to nominal wages and to SRAS.

rubric.point: Explains that, with unemployment above the natural rate, nominal wages and other input prices fall
accept: input prices or production costs fall because of the high unemployment
wages fall as the oil price shock fades and workers are plentiful

rubric.point: States that SRAS then shifts to the right until real output returns to full employment (YF)
accept: the SRPC shifts back to the left toward SRPC1, if linked to SRAS shifting right

parts.sample: With unemployment above the natural rate, many workers are looking for jobs, so nominal wages and other input prices fall over time. Lower costs shift SRAS to the right, back toward SRAS1, until AD and SRAS cross on LRAS and real output returns to full employment. On the Phillips curve graph, SRPC2 shifts back left to SRPC1.

parts.label: E
parts.prompt: Assume expected inflation in Velmar is still 2 percent. Identify Velmar's unemployment rate and inflation rate at the new long-run equilibrium.

rubric.point: Unemployment of 5 percent and inflation of 2 percent (back at point A, on LRPC)
accept: the natural rate and the expected inflation rate

parts.sample: In the long run Velmar returns to point A: unemployment is 5 percent, the natural rate, and inflation is 2 percent, the expected rate.
